candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44(d) require limits in addition to, or more stringent than effluent limitation guidelines (technology based). NM WQS that are more stringent than effluent limitation guideline and applicable for this discharge are based on 20.6.4 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether water-quality-based limits under 20.6.4 NMAC are required and enforceable for this discharge determines if numeric WQS limits must be selected instead of or in addition to technology-based limits when evaluating reported measurements.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection a. pH
candidates.exact_span: Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS for pH, 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (s.u.), are more restrictive than the technology-based limits presented earlier and downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for pH (i.e., 5-9 s.u. for domestic water supply, 6.5-9 s.u. for agricultural water supply, etc.). The pH limits of 6.6 to 9.0 s.u. in the previous permit, which are protective of the downstream Navajo Nation standards, will be continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which pH standard is most restrictive (NM 6.6–9.0 s.u. versus downstream Navajo Nation values) or whether the continued draft-permit limits are the operative enforceable limits for FY2025 would change the numeric limit used for pH compliance comparisons.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: Primary contact currently is one of the designated uses of State of New Mexico Segment No. 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether primary contact remains a designated use (the word "currently") affects which WQS criteria and associated monitoring framework apply, changing both the selected bacteria limits and whether bacteria monitoring obligations are in force.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: The State of New Mexico WQS criteria applicable to the primary contact designated use of the receiving stream are the monthly geometric mean of E. coli bacteria of 126 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) and single sample of 410 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: These values are candidate enforceable numeric limits for E. coli; a different interpretation of their applicability to the discharge point or monitoring period would change which concentration thresholds are used to judge reported measurements.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: The results for E. coli may be reported as either colony forming units (CFU) or the most probable number (MPN) depending on the analytical method used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether reported CFU and MPN results are treated as directly comparable to the stated cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) limits affects how measurements are matched to numeric limits and whether a exceedance is found.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: The E. coli daily mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the TMDL was established
candidates.computation_change_reason: If this mass-loading limit is interpreted as an enforceable permit limit rather than background TMDL context, a different compliance test (mass per day versus concentration) would apply to available measurements.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: Daily mass loading limit, cfu/day = C, cfu/100 mL * 1,000 mL/L * l/0.264 gallons * Q, flow, expressed in 1,000,000 gallons/day
candidates.computation_change_reason: The formula defines how the mass-loading limit is derived; interpreting whether facility discharge flow or receiving-stream flow (see Q below) governs could change the computed applicable limit or whether a mass-loading comparison is possible.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span:
C = state water quality standard criterion for bacteria, 126 cfu/100 mL
Q = stream flow in million gallons per day (mgd), 299 MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether the 299 MGD stream-flow assumption is binding for permittee compliance, or how C maps to the operative single-sample versus geometric-mean criterion, would change the numeric mass-loading limit used in evaluation.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: Downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for E. coli bacteria are 126 cfu/100 mL monthly geometric mean for domestic water supply, and 235 cfu/100 mL to 575 cfu/100 mL single sample maximum for secondary human contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which downstream Navajo Nation criterion is controlling, or whether these standards require more stringent limits than NM primary-contact criteria, would change the selected numeric bacteria limits.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monthly geometric mean limit of 126 cfu/100 mL, daily maximum limit of 235 cfu/100 mL and daily maximum mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the previous permit will be continued in the draft permit to be consistent with the New Mexico TMDL and protective of the more stringent NNWQS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states the permit limits to be continued but uses a 235 cfu/100 mL daily maximum where the NM primary-contact WQS above cites 410 cfu/100 mL single sample; resolving which value is the enforceable limit, and whether draft-continued limits govern FY2025, changes compliance comparisons.

candidates.locator: page 9, section fact_sheet, subsection b. Bacteria
candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monitoring frequency requirement in the previous permit be also continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a monitoring-frequency obligation carries forward from the previous permit into the operative permit affects which monitoring was required in FY2025 (Purpose B) and how missing or non-numeric results for expected bacteria monitoring should be classified when evidence of required sampling is indirect (Purpose C).
